subtitle: "Analysis of Electronic Health Records — Stage 2"

## Introduction

This script conducts the statistical analysis for a retrospective cohort study
evaluating the association between **proton pump inhibitor (PPI)** versus
**H2 receptor antagonist (H2RA)** prescription and subsequent **all-cause mortality**,
using simulated UK primary care electronic health record (EHR) data.

The analysis follows these key phases:
1. **Descriptive summaries**: Baseline patient characteristics (Table 1) and time-to-event metrics.
2. **Non-parametric survival analysis**: Kaplan-Meier estimation and log-rank tests.
3. **Cox regression modeling**:
   - Univariable (crude) hazard ratio estimation.
   - Multivariable modeling with functional form exploration (Martingale residuals and natural cubic splines for age).
   - Proportional hazards (PH) assumption diagnostics (log-log plots and Schoenfeld residuals).
   - Stratified Cox regression addressing non-proportionality across key covariates.
   - Extended Cox model incorporating a time-dependent effect (`tt()`).
4. **Predicted survival curves**: Estimated survival trajectories across specific clinical profiles.

**Pipeline stage:** 2 of 2 — run via `3_run_pipeline.R` (requires `analysis_data.Rds` generated by Stage 1).

## Section 2: Descriptive Statistics and Preliminary Analysis

### 2.1 Baseline cohort characteristics by exposure status (Table 1)

Convert exposure and clinical indicators to labeled factor variables for clean presentation,
and compile a publication-ready baseline characteristics table stratified by exposure group.
```{r}
# Group by exposure status and recode categorical indicators to factors
analysis_data <- analysis_data %>%
  mutate(
    ppi = factor(ppi, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("H2RA", "PPI")),
    prior_gcancer = factor(prior_gcancer, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    recent_gerd = factor(recent_gerd, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    recent_ulcer = factor(recent_ulcer, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    calendarperiod = factor(calendarperiod)
  )
levels(analysis_data$calendarperiod)

# Add binary treatment switching status indicator:
analysis_data <- analysis_data %>%
  mutate(
    switch_status = factor(
      ifelse(is.na(date_switch), "No", "Yes"),
      levels = c("No", "Yes")
    )
  )

# Generate baseline Table 1 using gtsummary and format with gt
tbl1 <- analysis_data %>%
  select(
    ppi,
    age,
    bmi, 
    n_contacts,
    gender,
    ses_person,
    eth5,
    calendarperiod,
    switch_status,
    prior_gcancer,
    recent_gerd,
    recent_ulcer
  ) %>%
  tbl_summary(
    by = ppi,
    type = list(
      switch_status ~ "categorical",
      prior_gcancer ~ "categorical",
      recent_gerd ~ "categorical",
      recent_ulcer ~ "categorical"
    ),
    statistic = list(
      all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd})",
      all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)"
    ),
    digits = list(
      all_continuous() ~ 1,
      all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1)
    ),
    label = list(
      age ~ "Age",
      bmi ~ "BMI",
      n_contacts ~ "Number of contacts",
      gender ~ "Gender",
      ses_person ~ "Socioeconomic status",
      eth5 ~ "Ethnicity",
      calendarperiod ~ "Calendar period",
      switch_status ~ "Switching",
      prior_gcancer ~ "Prior gastric cancer",
      recent_gerd ~ "Recent GERD",
      recent_ulcer ~ "Recent ulcer"
    ),
    missing = "no"
  ) %>%
  add_overall(last = FALSE) %>%
  bold_labels() %>%
  as_gt() %>%
    tab_header(
    title = md("**Cohort characteristics by exposure status**")
  )
tbl1

# Export Table 1
gtsave(tbl1, "2. Figures/table_baseline_characteristics.png")
```

### 2.2 Time-to-event and follow-up metrics

Calculate follow-up time in days and person-years, resolve zero follow-up times,
and tabulate event rates per 1,000 person-years across exposure arms.
```{r}
# Create follow-up time in days and years
analysis_data <- analysis_data %>%
  mutate(
    followup_time_days = as.numeric(enddate - indexdate),
    followup_time_years = followup_time_days / 365.25
  )

# Add a small amount to any zero follow-up times to avoid computational singularity in survival models
min_nonzero <- min(analysis_data$followup_time_days
                   [analysis_data$followup_time_days > 0], na.rm = TRUE)

analysis_data <- analysis_data %>%
  mutate(
    followup_time_days = ifelse(followup_time_days == 0, 
                                 min_nonzero / 2, followup_time_days),
    followup_time_years = followup_time_days / 365.25
  )

# Summarise time-to-event outcomes
tte_table <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(ppi) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    deaths_n = sum(died == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    deaths_pct = 100 * mean(died == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    censored_n = sum(died == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    censored_pct = 100 * mean(died == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_fu = median(followup_time_years, na.rm = TRUE),
    q1_fu = quantile(followup_time_years, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3_fu = quantile(followup_time_years, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_fu = sum(followup_time_years, na.rm = TRUE),
    event_rate = deaths_n / total_fu * 1000,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    `Deaths, n (%)` = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", format(deaths_n, big.mark = ","), deaths_pct),
    `Censored, n (%)` = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", format(censored_n, big.mark = ","), censored_pct),
    `Median follow-up (IQR), person-years` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f, %.1f)", median_fu, q1_fu, q3_fu),
    `Total follow-up, person-years` = round(total_fu, 1),
    `Death rate per 1,000 person-years` = round(event_rate, 1)
  ) %>%
  select(
    ppi, N, `Deaths, n (%)`, `Censored, n (%)`,
    `Median follow-up (IQR), person-years`,
    `Total follow-up, person-years`,
    `Death rate per 1,000 person-years`
  )

tte_gt <- tte_table %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Time-to-event summary by exposure group**")
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    ppi = "Treatment type" 
  ) %>%
    tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_column_labels(everything())
    )

tte_gt

gtsave(tte_gt, "2. Figures/table_time_to_event_summary.png")

# Exploratory distribution visualisations
ggplot(analysis_data, aes(followup_time_years, fill = ppi))+
  geom_histogram()

ggplot(analysis_data, aes(calendarperiod, fill = ppi)) +
  geom_bar()
# compare ppi groups
```

### 2.3 Kaplan-Meier survival curves and log-rank test

Estimate non-parametric survival functions overall and stratified by exposure arm,
accompanied by risk tables and formal log-rank testing.
```{r}
# Overall cohort survival
ppi_km_ov <- survfit(Surv(followup_time_years,died)~1,data=analysis_data)

ggsurvplot(ppi_km_ov, data = analysis_data,risk.table = T,conf.int = T)

# Kaplan-Meier curves stratified by exposure group (PPI vs H2RA)
ppi_km <- survfit(Surv(followup_time_years,died)~ppi,data=analysis_data)

km_plot <- ggsurvplot(
  ppi_km,
  data = analysis_data,
  risk.table = TRUE,
  risk.table.height = 0.30,
  conf.int = T,
  censor = FALSE,
  break.time.by = 5,
  xlab = "Time since first prescription (years)",
  ylab = "Survival probability",
  legend.title = "Exposure status",
  palette = c("turquoise3", "plum3"),
  ggtheme = theme_minimal(),
  risk.table.y.text = TRUE,
  risk.table.fontsize = 4
)

png("2. Figures/plot_kaplan_meier.png", width = 8, height = 7, units = "in", res = 300)
print(km_plot)
dev.off()

# Log-rank test (Null hypothesis: identical survival distributions across treatment groups)
logrank_test <- survdiff(Surv(followup_time_years,died)~ppi,data=analysis_data)

logrank_tab <- tibble(
  `Exposure status` = names(logrank_test$n),
  N = as.numeric(logrank_test$n),
  Observed = as.numeric(logrank_test$obs),
  Expected = round(as.numeric(logrank_test$exp), 0)
)

logrank_tab_gt <- logrank_tab %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Log-rank test: observed and expected deaths by exposure status**"),
    subtitle = md(
      paste0(
        "Chi-square = ", round(logrank_test$chisq, 2),
        ", df = ", length(logrank_test$n) - 1,
        ", p-value ",
        format.pval(
          1 - pchisq(logrank_test$chisq, df = length(logrank_test$n) - 1),
          digits = 3,
          eps = 0.001
        )
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_column_labels(everything())
  ) %>%
    tab_style(
    style = cell_text(size = px(18)),
    locations = cells_title(groups = "subtitle")
  )

logrank_tab_gt

gtsave(logrank_tab_gt, "2. Figures/table_logrank_test.png")
```

## Section 3: Cox Proportional Hazards Regression

### 3.1 Univariable (crude) Cox model for exposure
```{r}
# Crude association between exposure status and all-cause mortality
ppi_cox<-coxph(Surv(followup_time_years,died)~as.factor(ppi),data=analysis_data)
summary(ppi_cox)

# Extract tidy results for later combined table
cox_tab1 <- tidy(ppi_cox, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
```

### 3.2 Multivariable Cox modeling & functional form assessment

Assess the functional form of continuous covariates (`n_contacts` and `age`)
using Martingale residual plots and model fit criteria (AIC).
```{r}
# Preliminary inspection of continuous predictor distributions
hist(analysis_data$n_contacts)
hist(log(analysis_data$n_contacts))

# Reference multivariable model including all prospective confounders linearly
ppi_multi_cox<-coxph(Surv(followup_time_years,died)~ppi+age+as.factor(gender)+
                       as.factor(eth5)+as.factor(ses_person)+bmi+n_contacts +
                       as.factor(calendarperiod)+as.factor(prior_gcancer)+
                       as.factor(recent_gerd)+ as.factor(recent_ulcer),
                      data=analysis_data)

# ---- Linearity of healthcare contacts (n_contacts) ----
# Fit model excluding n_contacts and plot Martingale residuals against n_contacts
ppi_multi_cox1<-coxph(Surv(followup_time_years,died)~ppi+age+as.factor(gender)+
                       as.factor(eth5)+as.factor(ses_person)+bmi+
                       as.factor(calendarperiod)+as.factor(prior_gcancer)+
                       as.factor(recent_gerd)+ as.factor(recent_ulcer),
                      data=analysis_data)

mgale_cont<-resid(ppi_multi_cox1,type="martingale")

png("2. Figures/plot_martingale_residuals_contacts.png", width = 8, height = 7, units = "in", res = 300)
plot(analysis_data$n_contacts, mgale_cont,
     xlab = "Number of contacts",
     ylab = "Martingale residuals",
     pch = 16,
     col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.15))
lines(lowess(analysis_data$n_contacts, mgale_cont),
      col = "red", lwd = 4)
abline(h = 0, lwd = 2, col = "grey")
dev.off()

## Linearity assessment: LOWESS smoother appears approximately linear; modeled as linear term.

#-----------------------------------------------------------------------
# ---- Linearity and functional form of Age ----
# Fit model excluding age and plot Martingale residuals against age
ppi_multi_cox2<-coxph(Surv(followup_time_years,died)~ppi+n_contacts+as.factor(gender)+
                       as.factor(eth5)+as.factor(ses_person)+bmi+
                       as.factor(calendarperiod)+as.factor(prior_gcancer)+
                       as.factor(recent_gerd)+ as.factor(recent_ulcer),
                      data=analysis_data)

mgale_noage<-resid(ppi_multi_cox2,type="martingale")

png("2. Figures/plot_martingale_residuals_age.png", width = 8, height = 7, units = "in", res = 300)
plot(analysis_data$age, mgale_noage,
     xlab = "Age",
     ylab = "Martingale residuals",
     pch = 16,
     col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.15))
lines(lowess(analysis_data$age, mgale_noage),
      col = "red", lwd = 4)
abline(h = 0, lwd = 2, col = "grey")
dev.off()

# Martingale residuals reveal non-linearity; compare polynomial vs spline parameterisations
# Model with quadratic age:
ppi_multi_cox3<-coxph(Surv(followup_time_years,died)~ppi+n_contacts+as.factor(gender)+
                       as.factor(eth5)+as.factor(ses_person)+bmi+age+I(age^2)+
                       as.factor(calendarperiod)+as.factor(prior_gcancer)+
                       as.factor(recent_gerd)+ as.factor(recent_ulcer),
                      data=analysis_data)

# Model with natural cubic splines for age (3 degrees of freedom):
ppi_multi_cox4<-coxph(Surv(followup_time_years,died)~ppi+n_contacts+as.factor(gender)+
                       as.factor(eth5)+as.factor(ses_person)+bmi+ns(age,df=3)+
                       as.factor(calendarperiod)+as.factor(prior_gcancer)+
                       as.factor(recent_gerd)+ as.factor(recent_ulcer),
                      data=analysis_data)

# Model selection via Akaike Information Criterion (AIC):
aic_tab <- AIC(ppi_multi_cox, ppi_multi_cox3, ppi_multi_cox4) %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "Model") %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
   mutate(
    Model = c("Unadjusted", "Quadratic age model", "Spline age model")
  )

aic_tab

# Residual inspection following spline modeling for age
mgale_cont4<-resid(ppi_multi_cox4,type="martingale")

png("2. Figures/plot_martingale_residuals_agespline.png", width = 8, height = 7, units = "in", res = 300)
plot(analysis_data$age, mgale_cont4,
     xlab = "Age",
     ylab = "Martingale residuals",
     pch = 16,
     col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.15))
# Note: LOWESS call preserved as originally written
lines(lowess(analysis_data$n_contacts, mgale_cont),
      col = "red", lwd = 4)
abline(h = 0, lwd = 2, col = "grey")
dev.off()

## Model 4 (Natural cubic splines for age) selected for multivariable analysis based on AIC
cox_tab4 <- tidy(ppi_multi_cox4, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
cox_tab4
```

### 3.3 Consolidated results table (Univariable vs Multivariable Model 4)
```{r}
# Format univariable results
cox_tab1_df <- cox_tab1 %>%
  mutate(
    Model = "Single-variable model",
    Covariate = "PPI vs H2RA",
    `Hazard ratio` = round(estimate, 2),
    SE = round(std.error, 3),
    `95% CI` = paste0("(", round(conf.low, 2), ", ", round(conf.high, 2), ")"),
    `p-value` = format.pval(p.value, digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
  ) %>%
  select(Model, Covariate, `Hazard ratio`, SE, `95% CI`, `p-value`)

# Rename spline terms and categorical predictors for presentation
age_rows <- grepl("ns\\(age, df = 3\\)", cox_tab4$term)
cox_tab4$term[age_rows] <- paste("Age spline", seq_len(sum(age_rows)))

cox_tab4_df <- cox_tab4 %>%
  mutate(
    Model = "Multivariable model",
    Covariate = case_when(
      term == "ppiPPI" ~ "PPI",
      term == "n_contacts" ~ "Number of contacts",
      term == "bmi" ~ "BMI",
      term == "as.factor(gender)Male" ~ "Gender: Male",
      grepl("as.factor\\(eth5\\)", term) ~ sub("as.factor\\(eth5\\)", "Ethnicity: ", term),
      grepl("as.factor\\(ses_person\\)", term) ~ sub("as.factor\\(ses_person\\)", "Socioeconomic status: ", term),
      grepl("as.factor\\(calendarperiod\\)", term) ~ sub("as.factor\\(calendarperiod\\)", "Calendar period: ", term),
      grepl("as.factor\\(prior_gcancer\\)", term) ~ sub("as.factor\\(prior_gcancer\\)", "Prior gastric cancer: ", term),
      grepl("as.factor\\(recent_gerd\\)", term) ~ sub("as.factor\\(recent_gerd\\)", "Recent GERD: ", term),
      grepl("as.factor\\(recent_ulcer\\)", term) ~ sub("as.factor\\(recent_ulcer\\)", "Recent ulcer: ", term),
      TRUE ~ term
    ),
    `Hazard ratio` = round(estimate, 2),
    SE = round(std.error, 3),
    `95% CI` = paste0("(", round(conf.low, 2), ", ", round(conf.high, 2), ")"),
    `p-value` = format.pval(p.value, digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
  ) %>%
  select(Model, Covariate, `Hazard ratio`, SE, `95% CI`, `p-value`)

# Combine both models into a single structured gt table
combined_cox_table <- bind_rows(cox_tab1_df, cox_tab4_df) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Model") %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Cox regression models**")
  ) %>%
  tab_options(row_group.font.weight = "bold") %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_column_labels(everything())
  )

combined_cox_table
gtsave(combined_cox_table, "2. Figures/table_cox_regression_combined.png")
```

## Section 4: Evaluation of Proportional Hazards (PH) Assumption

### 4.1 Log-minus-log survival curves
```{r}
# Visual assessment of parallelism in log-minus-log survival plots
log_test <- survfit(Surv(followup_time_years, died) ~ ppi, data = analysis_data)

png("2. Figures/plot_log_log_survival.png", width = 8, height = 7, units = "in", res = 300)
plot(log_test,
     fun = "cloglog",
     col = c("black", "red"),
     lty = 1:2,
     lwd = 2,
     xlab = "log(Time)",
     ylab = "log(-log(Survival))",
     main = "Log-minus-log survival plot by exposure")

legend("topleft",
       legend = levels(as.factor(analysis_data$ppi)),
       col = c("black", "red"),
       lty = 1:2,
       lwd = 2)
dev.off()
```

### 4.2 Scaled Schoenfeld residuals test
```{r}
# Formal test of proportional hazards assumption via Schoenfeld residuals
prop_test <- cox.zph(ppi_multi_cox4, transform = "identity")
prop_test
par(mfrow=c(2,2))
plot(prop_test,col="red",lwd=2)

# Individual diagnostic plots for covariates exhibiting PH violations
png("2. Figures/plot_schoenfeld_residuals_ppi.png", width = 8, height = 7, units = "in", res = 300)
plot(prop_test[1], resid = TRUE, se = TRUE,
     col = "red", lwd = 2,
     xlab = "Time",
     ylab = "Scaled Schoenfeld residuals",
     main = "PPI")
dev.off()

png("2. Figures/plot_schoenfeld_residuals_gender.png", width = 8, height = 7, units = "in", res = 300)
plot(prop_test[3], resid = TRUE, se = TRUE,
     col = "red", lwd = 2,
     xlab = "Time",
     ylab = "Scaled Schoenfeld residuals",
     main = "Gender")
dev.off()

png("2. Figures/plot_schoenfeld_residuals_ses.png", width = 8, height = 7, units = "in", res = 300)
plot(prop_test[5], resid = TRUE, se = TRUE,
     col = "red", lwd = 2,
     xlab = "Time",
     ylab = "Scaled Schoenfeld residuals",
     main = "SES")
dev.off()

png("2. Figures/plot_schoenfeld_residuals_calendar_period.png", width = 8, height = 7, units = "in", res = 300)
plot(prop_test[8], resid = TRUE, se = TRUE,
     col = "red", lwd = 2,
     xlab = "Time",
     ylab = "Scaled Schoenfeld residuals",
     main = "Calender period")
dev.off()
```

## Section 5: Stratified and Extended Cox Models

Three categorical covariates showed evidence of non-proportional hazards:
- `gender` ($p = 8.2 \times 10^{-8}$)
- `ses_person` ($p = 0.0065$)
- `calendarperiod` ($p = 3.3 \times 10^{-16}$)

We evaluate stratified Cox models to allow separate baseline hazard functions across these strata.

### 5.1 Stratified Cox models
```{r}
## Stratified model 1: Stratified on all three violating covariates
ppi_strat1 <- coxph(Surv(time = followup_time_years, event = died) ~ ppi + 
                     n_contacts + bmi + ns(age, 3) +
    as.factor(eth5) + as.factor(prior_gcancer) +
    as.factor(recent_gerd) + as.factor(recent_ulcer) +
    strata(gender) +
    strata(ses_person) +
    strata(calendarperiod),
  data = analysis_data
)

summary(ppi_strat1)

## Stratified model 2: Stratified on gender and calendar period only (SES modeled parametrically)
ppi_strat2 <- coxph(Surv(time = followup_time_years, event = died) ~ ppi + 
                     n_contacts + bmi + ns(age, 3) +
    as.factor(eth5) + as.factor(prior_gcancer) +
    as.factor(recent_gerd) + as.factor(recent_ulcer) +
    strata(gender) +
    as.factor(ses_person) +
    strata(calendarperiod),
  data = analysis_data
)

summary(ppi_strat2)

## Check AIC between stratification options
AIC(ppi_strat1, ppi_strat2)

# Residual diagnostics for Stratified Model 1
prop_test10 <- cox.zph(ppi_strat1, transform = "identity")
plot(prop_test10, col = "red")

png("2. Figures/plot_schoenfeld_residuals_post_stratification.png", width = 8, height = 7, units = "in", res = 300)
plot(prop_test10[1], resid = TRUE, se = TRUE,
     col = "red", lwd = 2,
     xlab = "Time",
     ylab = "Scaled Schoenfeld residuals",
     main = "PPI-post adjustment")
dev.off()

# STRAT1 demonstrates superior fit (lower AIC).
# Non-proportionality for PPI exposure remains significant, prompting an extended model with a time-varying coefficient.
```

### 5.2 Extended Cox model with time-varying covariate effect (`tt()`)
```{r}
## Recode PPI as 0/1 numeric for the time-transform function
analysis_data <- analysis_data %>%
  mutate(ppi_num = ifelse(ppi == "PPI", 1, 0))

# Extended Cox model with time-varying PPI coefficient: beta(t) = beta_0 + beta_1 * log(t + 0.1)
ppi_strat3 <- coxph(Surv(time = followup_time_years, event = died) ~ ppi_num + 
                     n_contacts + bmi + ns(age, 3) +
    as.factor(eth5) + as.factor(prior_gcancer) +
    as.factor(recent_gerd) + as.factor(recent_ulcer) +
    strata(gender) +
    strata(ses_person) +
    strata(calendarperiod) +
      tt(ppi_num),
  data = analysis_data,
  tt = function(x, t, ...) x * log(t+0.1))

summary(ppi_strat3)

# Stratified model without time-varying effect for comparison
ppi_strat4 <- coxph(Surv(time = followup_time_years, event = died) ~ ppi_num + 
                     n_contacts + bmi + ns(age, 3) +
    as.factor(eth5) + as.factor(prior_gcancer) +
    as.factor(recent_gerd) + as.factor(recent_ulcer) +
    strata(gender) +
    strata(ses_person) +
    strata(calendarperiod),
  data = analysis_data
)

summary(ppi_strat4)

# AIC comparison between constant vs time-varying PPI models
AIC(ppi_strat3, ppi_strat4)
```

#### Final model selection
```{r}
# ppi_strat3 represents the fully adjusted, stratified extended Cox model
```

## Section 6: Estimated Survivor Curves for Patient Profiles

Predict survivor trajectories from the stratified model (`ppi_strat1`) for four representative clinical profiles:
- **Profile a:** Male, age 60, White, no comorbidities, most deprived quintile (SES 5).
- **Profile b:** Male, age 60, White, peptic ulcer, least deprived quintile (SES 1).
- **Profile c:** Female, age 60, White, no comorbidities, most deprived quintile (SES 5).
- **Profile d:** Female, age 60, White, peptic ulcer, least deprived quintile (SES 1).

Continuous covariates held at sample medians; calendar period fixed to 2005–2009.

```{r}
# Determine reference covariate values (sample medians and modes)
med_contacts <- median(analysis_data$n_contacts) # 4
med_bmi <- median(analysis_data$bmi)             # 27.5
table(analysis_data$prior_gcancer)               # No
table(analysis_data$recent_gerd)                 # No
```

```{r}
# Construct prediction data frame across all 8 profile-exposure combinations
newdata <- data.frame(
  ppi = factor(c("H2RA", "PPI", "H2RA", "PPI", "H2RA", "PPI", "H2RA", "PPI"),
               levels = levels(analysis_data$ppi)),
  age = c(60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60),
  n_contacts = rep(med_contacts, 8),
  bmi = rep(med_bmi, 8),
  eth5 = factor(rep("White", 8), levels = levels(analysis_data$eth5)),
  prior_gcancer = factor(c("No", "No", "No", "No", "No", "No", "No", "No"),
                         levels = levels(analysis_data$prior_gcancer)),
  recent_gerd = factor(c("No", "No", "No", "No", "No", "No", "No", "No"),
                       levels = levels(analysis_data$recent_gerd)),
  recent_ulcer = factor(c("No", "No", "Yes", "Yes", "No", "No", "Yes", "Yes"),
                        levels = levels(analysis_data$recent_ulcer)),
  gender = factor(c("Male", "Male", "Male", "Male", "Female", "Female", "Female", "Female"),
                  levels = levels(analysis_data$gender)),
  ses_person = factor(c("Most Deprived (5)", "Most Deprived (5)",
                        "Least Deprived (1)", "Least Deprived (1)",
                        "Most Deprived (5)", "Most Deprived (5)",
                        "Least Deprived (1)", "Least Deprived (1)"),
                      levels = levels(analysis_data$ses_person)),
  calendarperiod = factor(rep("2005-2009", 8), levels = levels(analysis_data$calendarperiod))
)

# Compute estimated survival curves
sf <- survfit(ppi_strat1, newdata = newdata)

# Plot and export survival curves
png("2. Figures/plot_cox_predicted_survivor_curves.png", width = 8, height = 7, units = "in", res = 300)

plot(sf,
     mark.time = FALSE,
     conf.int = F,
     col = c("black", "black", "springgreen4", "springgreen4", "blue", "blue", "firebrick", "firebrick"),
     lty = c(1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2),
     lwd = 2,
     ylim = c(0, 1),
     xlim = c(0, 12),
     xlab = "Time since first prescription (Years)",
     ylab = "Survival probability",
     main = "Estimated survivor curves by exposure status for individual profiles")

legend("bottomleft",
       legend = c(
         "a: H2RA", "a: PPI",
         "b: H2RA", "b: PPI",
         "c: H2RA", "c: PPI",
         "d: H2RA", "d: PPI"
       ),
       col = c("black", "black", "springgreen4", "springgreen4", "blue", "blue", "firebrick", "firebrick"),
       lty = c(1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2),
       lwd = 2,
       cex = 0.8)

dev.off()
```
